newsitem.title: USA: CBOT new crop corn surges higher on hot weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT new crop corn surges higher on hot weather.

text.p: CBOT corn futures surged higher in fast trade, led by new crop months on forecasts for hot, dry weather in the U.S. Midwest, traders said.

A heat wave was forecast for the U.S. Midwest through Friday with high temperatures ranging from the low to high 90 degrees Fahrenheit area, beginning Tuesday, meteorologists said. No rainfall was expected until Friday.

Hot, dry weather during pollination can cut yields, traders said. Some pockets of eastern Iowa and central Illinois have been in need of moisture and meteorologists said Monday's showers may have missed those areas.
At 1009 CDT, corn was up 6-1/4 to 4-3/4 cents per bushel with December up five cents at $2.54 a bushel.
